reason: The cited evidence (E1–E3) supports that a nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50 gives ultralow wear, but it does not address laser surface alloying as the fabrication method, nor does it provide any evidence for a post-treatment stabilization step or the claimed 30–50% friction reduction.
premises: Laser surface alloying can create a nanohierarchical microstructure with composition undulation in Ni50(AlNbTiV)50
A nanohierarchical architecture with composition undulation yields ultralow wear rate from RT to 800 °C
Nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates provide adaptive friction interface protection
A post-treatment stabilization step can preserve the nanostructure against high-temperature coarsening
The treated alloy will show 30–50% reduction in friction and wear versus untreated alloy
